question:
**Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the italicised words in the given sentence.**

I have been a vegetarian for *a very long time*.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Donkey’s years**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let us look at the meaning of the given idioms.
 
 
• **Donkey’s years**: A very long time.
 
• **Duck in the thunderstorm**: Looking hopelessly sad and dejected.
 
• **Die in harness**: To die while still working or on duty or before retirement.
 
• **Damocles’ sword**: Any situation threatening imminent harm or disaster.
 
 
 
• So, as per the meaning of the given idioms "**Donkey’s years**" is the most appropriate option.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__**

 
• The idiomatic expression **"donkey's years" **is used in English to denote a very long time.
 
• The phrase originates from the idea that donkeys live a long time, and also from rhyming slang where **"years" **rhymes with **"donkey ears."**
 
• In Hindi, the closest expression may be **"बहुत समय", **meaning a lot of time, or **"लंबे समय तक", **meaning for a long time.
 
 
• Example: "I haven't seen you in donkey's years!"
 
• This means I haven't seen you for a very long time.
 
 
 
• In Hindi, you might express it like: "मुझे लगता है कि मैंने तुम्हें बहुत समय से नहीं देखा है!"
 
 
• This means I feel I haven't seen you for a very long time.
